chunks: Regarding two witnesses who testified against a woman that her husband had divorced her, and so she remarried, then her husband came and denied the divorce —

he said: 'They shall both be given the legal penalty (hadd), and both shall be liable for the dowry (mahr) to the husband. Then she shall observe the waiting period ('iddah), then return to her first husband.'

key_terms.الصَّدَاقَ: Sadaq/Mahr — the obligatory bridal gift paid by the husband to his wife upon marriage; here the witnesses must compensate the first husband for the mahr he effectively lost
key_terms.الطَّلَاقَ: Talaq — Islamic divorce pronounced by the husband
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: Hadd — the Quranically prescribed fixed legal penalty; in this context, the hadd for false accusation (qadhf) of 80 lashes
key_terms.تَعْتَدُّ: 'Iddah — the mandatory waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or the death of her husband before she may remarry

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on false witnesses who testify that a husband divorced his wife?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on the case of two witnesses who falsely testified that a woman's husband had divorced her, enabling her to remarry. When the husband returns and denies the divorce, the witnesses face criminal liability (hadd for false accusation) and financial liability (reimbursing the mahr to the first husband), while the woman must complete the 'iddah (waiting period) from the second marriage and then return to her first husband. This ruling illustrates the Shia jurisprudential approach to false testimony in matrimonial matters, emphasizing both penal and civil consequences for perjurers.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding two witnesses testifying upon a woman that her husband has divorced her. So she re-married. Then her husband came and denied the divorce.

Heasws said: ‘They would both be whipped the legal penalty (Hadd), and would both be responsible for the dowry to the husband. Then she would observe the waiting period, then return to her first husband’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid who has narrated the following: “About the case of two witnesses who testify for a woman that her husband has divorced her and she marries; but her husband comes and denies the divorce, he (the Imam) has said, ‘
The two must be subjected to penalty and held responsible for the mahr (dower) in favor of the husband; then she is returned to the first husband.’”
